source_note: Captured via F2 on 2026-09-12 while playing arcade Mortal Kombat II, right after winning a match.
roi_reason: Added 2026-10-11: hashed over the whole frame, mk2__press_start_to_kontinue and mk2__prepare_for_next_kombat were only 20 bits apart (match threshold 24) - the shared MK II backdrop dominated the hash, so a slightly different live frame of one could be read as the other. Cropped to Player 1's panel, where the two actually differ, they're 78 bits apart. Caught by tests/test_screen_library.py::test_no_two_screens_are_confusable.
notes: Post-match transition screen: Player 1's panel (left) reads 'PREPARE FOR YOUR NEXT KOMBAT'; a Player 2 panel is visible at the right capture edge but its text is cut off ('PRESS'/'...TO...KONT...' fragments only) - left out of canonical_text since it isn't fully legible. A later capture the same session (mk2__press_start_to_kontinue) shows the same Player 1 panel later reading 'PRESS START TO KONTINUE' instead - these are two different states of what appears to be the same continue/next-opponent sequence, not two views of one fixed screen.
